what_its_for: Nintedanib is used to treat certain lung diseases that cause scarring in the lungs, including idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a type of chronic lung disease that makes it harder to breathe over time. It is also used for lung scarring related to autoimmune diseases (like scleroderma) and for a certain type of lung cancer. It works by slowing down the process that causes scar tissue to build up in the lungs.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsule. Take it WITH food (with a meal) to help reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time — do not double up.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg (one capsule) taken TWICE a day, about 12 hours apart (for example, once with breakfast and once with dinner). Your doctor may lower your dose to 100 mg twice a day if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose completely. Take your next regular dose at its scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time or extra doses to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep capsules in their original packaging (blister pack) to protect them from moisture and light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use capsules that are past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking, as it can make your lung disease worse and reduce how well the medicine works. Avoid drinking alcohol or limit it, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medication — it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after stopping. Avoid taking St. John's Wort (a herbal supplement) as it can make nintedanib less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), severe stomach or abdominal pain, vomiting blood or dark tarry stools (signs of bleeding), sudden severe headache, vision changes, or weakness on one side of your body (signs of blood clot or stroke), difficulty breathing that gets suddenly worse, or signs of a heart attack such as chest pain or pressure. Also contact your doctor if you have persistent nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not improve, unexplained weight loss, or signs of infection such as fever or chills. Women who become pregnant while taking this medication should call their doctor immediately.
when_it_works: Nintedanib does not cure your lung disease, but it helps slow down how fast the scarring gets worse. You may not feel different right away. It usually takes several months of regular use before you and your doctor can tell if the medicine is working. It is very important to keep taking it every day, even if you do not notice a difference in how you feel. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use during pregnancy. It can seriously harm or cause birth defects in an unborn baby. Use reliable contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. It is not known if nintedanib passes into breast milk but could harm a nursing baby. Liver problems: Your doctor will check your liver before and during treatment. If you have liver disease, your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Elderly patients (65 and older): Older adults may be more likely to experience side effects, especially diarrhea. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: This medication is not approved for use in children.
